**Verdict: keep Whodunit, but as it stands today it would lose.** The idea is sound and nobody else has its core, but nothing a judge can see exists yet. My reviewer scored it 42/100 on the official weights, which puts it around 20th of the 140 public entries.

Three things could not be checked: rivals' X posts (X returns 200 for any ID), their videos (links confirmed, not watched), and their neatlogs trace links (login-gated). All scores are my reviewers' reading of the repos, not the judges'.

## Where we stand today

| Entry | Score | Whodunit today (42) is |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| FirstRun | 89 | 53% worse |
| Release Gate | 77 | 45% worse |
| Verbatim, Cair, Crashtest, Mend | 72–73 | 42% worse |
| HiOffer | 70 | 40% worse |
| VeriFix | 67 | 37% worse |
| Niyam, Night Shift | 57–63 | about 30% worse |
| AgentBisect, Autopsy (direct rivals) | 39 | 8% better |
| Rootline (direct rival) | 37 | 14% better |

The gap is almost entirely packaging, which is 60% of the score:

| Criterion | Weight | Whodunit | FirstRun |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| The agent | 30% | 7.5 | 9 |
| neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | 4 | 10 |
| Demo video | 20% | 0 | 8 |
| Building in public | 15% | 1 | 9 |
| Usefulness, originality | 10% | 8 | 8 |

If the plan below lands, my estimate is 75–85. That beats everyone except FirstRun, which would still be about 10% ahead. A top-three finish is realistic; I can't promise first.

## What the rival research found

- **Our technical lead is real but narrow.** No other entry handles failures that happen only some of the time. AgentBisect, the only other entry that replays across commits, uses fixed pass-rate thresholds and named 1 of its 3 planted bugs with 2 wrong accusations (ours: 5 of 5, none wrong).
- **Night Shift tells nearly our story.** It goes bad commit, Entire prompt, dollar damage, verified fix, with a live hosted app and cfo.ai as a runtime input. It has no video or posts yet.
- **Rivals have things we lack:**
  - public cfo.ai links;
  - clickable Entire and neatlogs evidence;
  - live demos;
  - real external targets (FirstRun has four upstream PRs);
  - results written back into neatlogs;
  - starting an investigation from a single production trace.
- **Our own repo has problems a judge would catch:**
  - The headline brief says the bug is "deterministic" while its page says 81%.
  - A fix is called "proven" although a fix that still fails 4% of the time passes that test about a third of the time.
  - Gateway errors and timeouts count as failures, so one provider burst can frame a commit.
  - Fix checks replay only the failing inputs, so a patch that broke all refunds would pass.
  - The README says 41 commits; no case has 41.
  - The pitch says "neatlogs" where the data is in local neatroots.
  - The build log names and grades other teams.
  - CI will likely fail on first push, because the fix step commits with no git identity.

## Revised plan, in order

1. **Today, now:** post the first #neatHack post with a screenshot. It needs no public repo, and this criterion is worth 15% and sits at 1.
2. **Today:** sign in to cfo.ai and build the model (three scenarios, lever simulator, public link). Add one real write from code so damages land in the model.
3. **Today:** consistency pass on every error above. Reword "proven" to what the numbers support.
4. **Tonight, technical upgrades:**
   - trace Whodunit's own investigation to neatlogs cloud and write the verdict back;
   - start a case from one neatlogs trace id;
   - void infrastructure errors and retry;
   - add a "does no harm" check that replays the other cases on each fix;
   - add a "no commit did it" arm for model or dependency drift;
   - add two-culprit detection, tested in the simulator first.
5. **Overnight, time-boxed to 4 hours:** one real regression in a public open-source agent's history. This is the biggest credibility gain; drop it if nothing reproduces.
6. **Monday morning:** design revamp, go public, casebook on GitHub Pages, checkpoint links.
7. **Monday 1–5 PM:** the video, with three protected hours. Submit at 7:00 PM sharp, because the organisers engage with the first 50 submission posts.

Cut the AWS replay worker and Entire Brain.

## Design revamp

The page reads as a dark dashboard in every screenshot, so the paper metaphor is invisible.

- **Light paper by default,** with all evidence re-shot.
- **The lineup becomes the hero:** a numbered strip of suspects, cleared ones struck through, replays as typed x and o, the culprit ringed in red pencil, animated round by round for the video.
- **A real stamp:** large, rotated, "CASE CLOSED" in red and "OPEN, NOT FIXED" in ink.
- **A typed header form** with dotted leaders for suspects, replays and cost.
- **Citations as footnotes,** replacing the chips after every sentence.
- **Evidence as Exhibit A and B,** with the first diverging step in red.
- **Damages lead with the money.**
- **The casebook becomes a docket,** one stamped row per case.
- **Remove the model name** printed on every page.

## Before anything is pushed

This research session got attached to a checkpoint. Entire took it into checkpoint `86a62151581b` when another session committed `ceaa74f` at 1:17 PM, so my warning last night was right but too weak. That checkpoint holds your private notes and today's rival research.

Four older checkpoints also contain rival notes: `587df29ec38f`, `b7aa968e95c5`, `e4d86ea17901` and `feaef2731ecd`. `refs/private-backup/checkpoints-before-purge` must never be pushed either, so no `--mirror`. Nothing has left your machine, and I changed nothing in the repo.

## Decisions for you

1. **When to go public.** I recommend scrubbing tonight, pushing to a private GitHub repo to test CI, and flipping to public Monday 9 AM. Going public today would give more hours of clickable evidence, but Night Shift's own log says it chose its concept after reading rival repos.
2. **Should I write the paste-ready prompt for the build session?** It would cover steps 3, 4 and 6 with no rival names in it, since that session is recorded.
